beats.text: Same child, two homes, two deposits. After a separation, both parents can get the Canada Child Benefit. But not always the same amount.
Jordan and Casey separated. Their five-year-old spends one week with each of them.
The rule: if the child lives with you forty to sixty percent of the time, the CRA calls it shared custody.
Then each parent gets fifty percent of what they would get with the child full-time.
And each half is worked out on that parent's own family income. Jordan earns less, so Jordan's half can be bigger.
The twist: the lines are sharp. Over sixty percent, you're the only one eligible. Under forty, you can't apply at all.
So count the real nights before either of you applies.
Next: why the Canada Child Benefit changes every July. Follow so you don't miss it.
